answer: Agents must stake a scarce on-chain credential minted only after completing a unique physical-world task, such as submitting a verified geolocation-tagged photo of a shale outcrop. Each credential carries a plume watermark tying it to one biometric signer, and reputation is a thread linking that signer across epochs. Duplicating an identity requires acquiring another credential, biometric, and stake, making mass sybils prohibitively expensive while honest agents trade freely.
